transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-17
Time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Tom Reed (Oakbridge - Head of Search), Maya Lopez (Oakbridge - ML Engineer), Evan Clark (Oakbridge - CTO)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on embeddings / reranking. Oakbridge currently uses ElasticSearch for lexicographic search + Pinecone for vectors. They want to reduce tail latency and cost during peak, explore hybrid BM25 + ANN rerank, and evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private because of data residency and compliance.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Alex from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Tom: Good, thanks. Morning. Appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:11] Evan: Morning. Quick agenda we want to walk you through our current stack, pain points, and see what Redwood recommends for embeddings/reranking.
[00:20] Alex: Perfect. Priya, want to run the technical questions?
[00:22] Priya: Sure. Tom, can you give us a snapshot: what does the pipeline look like today?
[00:28] Tom: Yeah. So we have ElasticSearch for core retrieval, which handles BM25. For semantic matching we've started storing vectors in Pinecone. Right now our embeddings are OpenAI ada-style, 1536 dims, batch embeddings via a small job. Rerank happens in-app: we pull top 200 from ES, then top 50 from Pinecone, run a fine-tuned cross-encoder for final ranking.
[00:49] Maya: The cross-encoder is pretty expensive, and it's our biggest cost during peak. Also latency spikes when re-ranking a large candidate set.
[00:56] Priya: Got it. What's peak load like? QPS, concurrency?
[00:59] Tom: Average queries per second is around 30, peak maybe 100 QPS during sale events. Concurrency high  spikes to 200 concurrent requests. Candidate set sizes are 50-200 depending on query.
[01:15] Priya: That's helpful. Are you doing hybrid search  meaning do you combine BM25 and vector scores before rerank?
[01:20] Tom: We are, yes. We run BM25, then union with ANN from Pinecone, dedupe, then feed to the cross-encoder. We're exploring if moving more of that into a single service helps with latency.
[01:29] Alex: When you say Pinecone, do you have concerns about vendor lock or control? Any compliance/regulatory constraints?
[01:34] Evan: Mainly data residency for EU customers and corporate security. We're SOC2 Type II in progress, and we need KMS-managed keys for any private deployment. For some enterprise clients we may need on-prem or VPC options.
[01:46] Alex: Understood  Redwood has Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For high QPS and predictable latency, Dedicated or Private usually works best. Hosted is faster to get started but has multi-tenant characteristics that matter for strict isolation.
[01:56] Tom: Can you run through the tradeoffs? Cost per token, latency, and whether you support connectors to Pinecone / Milvus or we need to move vectors?
[02:04] Priya: Sure. High level: Hosted API is turnkey  simple REST/SDK, streaming, etc. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and lower per-token cost because you can pack capacity. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you customer-managed network, KMS integration, and audit logs. For connectors: Redwood supports feeding vectors into most vector DBs via batch exports and we have direct integrations to push/pull with Pinecone, Milvus, and Weaviate; but many customers choose to consolidate and let Redwood serve vectors directly to avoid cross-network hops.
[02:36] Maya: If we keep Pinecone, is there extra latency?
[02:39] Priya: There can be an added network hop; it depends on co-location and whether the vector DB supports the throughput. For 100 QPS and 200 candidate sets, we often recommend colocating or using dedicated Redwood-backed indexing to avoid the extra RTTs. Also Redwood's KV/prefix caching can reduce repeated work.
[02:58] Tom: Okay. What about dimensionality? We're on 1536 today. Could we reduce dims to 768 to save cost without hurting quality?
[03:06] Priya: Potentially, but it depends on your model and evals. We typically suggest running a quick ablation: downsample embeddings or try a smaller model (1536 -> 768) and run A/B on your rerank metrics (MRR, NDCG). Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization or dimensionality reduction profiles.
[03:24] Evan: Any quantization options? We run many candidates through a cross-encoder that costs CPU cycles  if embeddings are quantized, does that help?
[03:30] Priya: Yes  Redwood's serving runtime supports int8 and some quantized-aware kernels which reduce memory and increase throughput for ANN. That doesn't directly change cross-encoder cost though; it helps the vector search step much more. For cross-encoder, you can move to a distilled reranker or tiered approach: run a lightweight re-ranker first, then the expensive model on top-k.
[03:50] Tom: What's a reasonable candidate set size to feed the cross-encoder after tiering?
[03:55] Priya: Often 20-50 for a production rerank. You can do two-stage: cheap bi-encoder to narrow 200 -> 50, then cross-encoder 50 -> final. That keeps latency predictable.
[04:06] Maya: For the POC we'd like to try: 1) Redwood Hosted embeddings for quick proof, 2) Dedicated sizing for production if latency looks good, and 3) Private option if we need EU-only data residency. Does that flow make sense?
[04:17] Alex: Absolutely. For POC we can provision Hosted and a small Dedicated estimate. We'll share a sizing spreadsheet  Priya, can we map their QPS and candidate sizes to GPU types (A10G vs A100) and expected latency?
[04:28] Priya: Yup. Roughly, for a GPU-backed cross-encoder at 50 concurrency you'd look at A10G or T4 for cost-conscious setups and A100/80GB for heavy throughput and lowest latency. For ANN and embeddings, CPU-backed pools can be cheaper when using quantized indexes, but Dedicated GPU gives predictable pkgs. We'll include cost per 1M queries and tail latency estimates.
[04:51] Evan: Any specifics on authentication and SSO? We need SAML and SCIM sync for user provisioning.
[04:55] Alex: We support SAML SSO, SCIM tooling for user provision, and RBAC at the project/token level. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management and provide audit logs.
[05:07] Tom: What about data retention can we configure retention windows and auto-delete?
[05:11] Priya: Yes, retention policies are configurable; for Hosted we have defaults but can support custom retention for enterprise customers. We'll document that in the SOC2+security pack.
[05:20] Maya: For the benchmarks, what artifacts do you need from us?
[05:22] Priya: A CSV of representative queries, ground truth relevance for eval (if available), current index sizes (#docs, avg doc length, number of fields), and traffic patterns (peak QPS, percentiles). We'll provide a template.
[05:34] Tom: We'll send that. Also curious if Redwood can integrate into our existing CI and deployment flow for model rollouts?
[05:40] Alex: Yes  Redwood Console supports rollouts, canary A/B, and you can pin model versions per route. We also surface token-level cost and latency.
[05:49] Evan: Good. One last thing  network egress costs and data flows for EU. If we go Hosted but regionally isolated, how do we ensure no EU data leaves EU?
[05:58] Priya: We have region selection and can provision hosts in EU regions; Dedicated/Private is the safest  Private VPC keeps traffic on customer network and on-prem option exists for air-gapped needs. We'll include network diagram differentiators in the doc pack.
[06:11] Tom: Awesome. Any immediate blockers?
[06:13] Alex: Not from our side. We'll get the pricing and bench template over this week. From Oakbridge: share the query CSV and index stats.
[06:21] Maya: We'll aim to send that by Friday.
[06:23] Alex: Great. Quick recap of next steps and owners...
[06:27] (recap and thanks)
[06:30] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[06:31] Alex: Thanks  we'll follow up with the deck and POC plan.
[06:35] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings  references to "KV cache" might appear as "K V cache" and Redwood product names sometimes abbreviated (Redwood Dedicated / Redwood Private). There's a few filler words and overlapping talk around 03:00-04:00 when we discussed quantization.
